miniProject.title: Native run-duration histogram with a strict pybind11 binding and a sanitizer-backed repair
miniProject.brief: Move the run-duration histogram into C++ behind a strict Python boundary. Build it with CMake in debug, release and sanitizer trees, test it against NumPy, and follow one sanitizer report from evidence to regression test.
steps: Write the histogram core over spans with an owning `Histogram` class, and test copy independence, moves and bounds errors in a native test executable, using the AlgoMaster RAII and Copy-and-Swap Idiom exercises as reference.
Seed an off-by-one that overflows the bins, capture the sanitizer report in a sanitizer build tree, repair it, connect the report to the frame with `gdb`, and keep the input as a regression test.
Test the histogram against `numpy.histogram` on random values and on values at and beside every edge, then adopt NumPy's edge rule or document and test your own.
Bind the core with pybind11 under dtype, shape, stride, alignment, ownership, exception and GIL contracts, and test every accepted and rejected input plus output lifetime.

Build debug, release and sanitizer trees with CMake following the CMake Tutorial building and testing steps and register the native tests with CTest, then document the exported symbols and linked libraries and diagnose one link or loader failure from its message.

Document the record layout from measured offsets, compare array-of-struct and struct-of-array scans with equal checksums, and split one call across threads with private bins merged after `join`, alongside a shared atomic-bin variant.
deliverables: The native component: core library, owning `Histogram`, native tests, extension module and CMake trees.
The sanitizer write-up with the preserved report, the `gdb` session and the regression test.
Binding and oracle tests plus a boundary note with symbols, libraries, the diagnosed failure and the layout comparison.

rubric.pass: The binding agrees with `numpy.histogram` on random data and at every edge, or a documented edge rule is tested instead.
rubric.strong: Edge cases come from a generator, and a naive index version is kept as a comparison that fails.

rubric.pass: Wrong dtype, lists, strided, reversed and multi-dimensional inputs are rejected with the stated exception types, and the result outlives the input.
rubric.strong: The binding names the owner of every buffer and the GIL state at each point.

rubric.pass: The report is preserved and explained, and the regression fails on the seeded code and passes after the repair.
rubric.strong: The write-up names what the sanitizers cannot prove here, such as a wrong but in-bounds bin.

rubric.pass: Debug, release and sanitizer trees build from scratch, CTest catches a false check, and one failure is diagnosed from its message.
rubric.strong: The note says which upgrades force a rebuild of the extension and why.

rubric.pass: Predicted offsets match the measured ones, both layouts agree, and raw timings are kept.
rubric.strong: The report separates the measured difference from cache explanations it did not test.

miniProject.feedsInto: The Python-native histogram, its sanitizer-backed repair and the evidence-first debugging report for the capstone.
